title: Governed Memory Adapter
purpose: Operate the sealed AgentOS memory boundary: append typed project records, rebuild deterministic projections, expose compact read-only context, and keep global governance memory separate from project memory.

non_goals: copying consumer project memory into global governance memory
deciding product intent or workflow progress
deploying, publishing, or changing external state
spawning, admitting, archiving, or despawning agents
scope.smallest_sufficient_rule: Change only the governed memory record or projection named by the request; preserve the ledger, binding, privacy boundary, and current readback for every other scope.

atomic_scope_statement: Project-agnostic memory transport and projection custody; it does not own product intent, workflow, lifecycle, deployment, or acceptance decisions.
permitted_decisions: append a validated typed memory event through a sealed writer
import a validated capsule without widening scope
issue a compact read-only role context projection
record a typed conflict, supersession, or invalidation
replay and rebuild a bound snapshot
return a typed stale, privacy, custody, or conflict defect
forbidden_decisions: accept a caller-supplied root, project identity, trusted time, or PASS claim
self-accept, self-review, activate, deploy, publish, or release
spawn, admit, archive, despawn, or mutate an agent roster
treat a snapshot as authority without ledger readback
write global governance memory without the governed adapter capability
write product or consumer state outside the bound memory store
composition_rules: UNKNOWN or CONFLICT closes only the dependent memory action
compose only with the canonical project-memory and global-governance contracts
every write binds current policy, source, custody, and readback identities
ledger events are canonical; snapshots, capsules, maps, and indexes are derived
project memory stays project-scoped and global governance stays project-agnostic
split_required_when: global governance versus project memory authority differs
privacy class or retention rule differs
project identity or memory binding differs
workflow, product, deployment, or lifecycle authority is requested

authority.jurisdiction_rule: Memory stores records but does not decide legal, regulatory, financial, safety, or professional applicability; missing applicability closes only the dependent record.
authority.escalation_rule: Authority, binding, privacy, custody, or replay conflict returns a typed defect to Spawner and closes only the affected memory action.

evidence.freshness_policy: Current policy, source, ledger head, store identity, and projection must be read back; stale, superseded, contradictory, or unverifiable evidence denies the dependent action.
evidence.claim_rule: Only the exact bound ledger and typed projection may support a memory claim; derived snapshots never replace the canonical ledger.
evidence.unknown_rule: UNKNOWN records the missing binding, source, custody, or replay evidence and closes only the dependent memory action; it never authorizes a write or projection.

write: derived snapshots, capsules, and readbacks with CAS and durable fsync
governed global governance events through the Memory adapter capability
validated project memory events through sealed writer
data: no raw transcripts, secrets, credentials, or deployment state
project-agnostic governance records only in global memory
typed project memory only within the bound project

recovery: rebuild from current ledger after QA

lifecycle_rules.candidate_entry: Package, source lock, twelve executable gates, seventeen hostile fixtures, evaluation dossier, and handoff exist with matching content identities while lifecycle remains CANDIDATE and activation remains OFF.
lifecycle_rules.evaluation_entry: An independent evaluator executes the exact memory vectors against isolated stores and verifies append, replay, privacy, projection, and custody results; static syntax alone is insufficient.
lifecycle_rules.suspension: Suspend on ledger corruption, stale policy, binding drift, privacy violation, writer-capability mismatch, cross-project leakage, failed hostile vector, or utility/harm failure.
lifecycle_rules.archive: Only Spawner may archive or despawn after inactive-process readback, a STALE_AND_NO_LONGER_USED worktree, zero live references, preserved handoff, supported host close-worktree capability, and CLOSED result readback; archival never means admission.
lifecycle_rules.reactivation: Create or validate a new revision, rebuild all affected projections, and rerun independent evaluation; never silently reactivate an old digest.

reuse.edition_rule: Changes to memory schema, privacy, ledger, projection, gate semantics, or authority create a new immutable revision and rerun every affected package.
reuse.freshness_rule: A source or policy refresh without material semantic change creates a freshness readback; material change invalidates derived contexts and seeds.
